result.rationale: The diff shows addGuests.handler.ts performing prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, with no transaction/rollback. If the calendar call fails, guests persist while the operation errors. On retry, uniqueGuests filters out emails already in booking.attendees, so uniqueGuests.length === 0 triggers TRPCError BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' — misleading for the user. The described mechanism is fully traceable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the Prisma update (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) occurs before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so the mutation can fail while the DB still has the newly-created attendees. A subsequent retry will compute `uniqueGuests` as empty because those emails are now in `booking.attendees`, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid` (`if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw ...`).
